author.name: William Faulkner
author.heading: About William Faulkner
author.bio: William Faulkner made his native Mississippi the setting for much of his fiction, including The Sound and the Fury and As I Lay Dying. His demanding style makes the recorded contrast with Hemingway’s vocabulary especially memorable, but its rhetorical force has also encouraged compression in later retellings.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Asked to rank contemporary writers, Faulkner put Hemingway fourth and criticized his willingness to take risks with language. The dictionary remark was part of that ranking, rather than a free-standing definition of good prose; later accounts often turn it into a tidier personal insult.
